column3: Everyday V-Neck Pima Cotton Blend T-Shirt
column21: Pima cotton is the difference between a white tee that survives a season and one that survives three. This is a foundation, not a feature.

column17: white, flax, deep navy, french blue + 9 others
column21: Thirteen colours, runs to 3X, and costs thirty-six dollars. European linen breathes properly in real heat rather than just looking as though it might.

column17: white, navy, true black, pale custard, taupe brown, caper, cafe au lait
column21: Textured cotton with a ruffled collar and cuff, so it is decidedly romantic rather than a neutral basic. Tagged for ruffles — if you have ruled those out, this is not your blouse.

column3: We The Free Perfect Oversized Long Sleeve Top
column17: white, black, forest biome, dusted cocoa + 4 others
column21: Dropped shoulders and soft cotton, cut to slouch on purpose. This is for the woman who finds a fitted tee makes her feel as though she is being inspected.
Box pleats give crisp poplin controlled volume rather than shapelessness. Best with something narrow underneath so the proportion reads deliberate.
Pintucking draws the eye vertically, which is quietly useful. Optic white rather than cream, so it sits properly against navy and dark denim.
Jersey that reads as a woven blouse, and the drape is what does it. Sizes 00 through 40 — the widest run anywhere in this slot.
Scoop neck, ruffled trim, unapologetically pretty. Tagged for both puff sleeves and ruffles, so it stays correctly hidden from anyone who has ruled those out.
Structured enough to replace a button-down in August, and sleeveless means no bulk under a jacket. It comes in petite, which sleeveless tops rarely do.

column3: By Anthropologie Short-Sleeve Lace-Trim Swing Blouse
column21: The swing shape moves when you do, and the lace trim stops it reading as a plain cotton top. Easy with jeans because it asks for no styling at all.

column3: By Anthropologie 100% Cotton Eyelet Popover Blouse
column21: Eyelet gives texture and airflow at the same time, which is why it has survived a century of summers. Feminine without needing a print to get there.
The most tailored shirt in this slot, and the stretch is why it stays tailored through a day of sitting down. The longer shirttail means it holds a tuck.
The Club C is the plainest court sneaker there is, and that is exactly why it works with everything. Leather, low, no branding shouting at you — buy it once and stop thinking about it.

column3: Ballet sneakers in suede and leather
column21: A ballet flat and a retro runner met in the middle, and the result is softer than either. The elasticated topline means no gaping at the ankle, and it comes with two sets of laces so you can change its mood.

column3: Women's Keds Champion Leather Lace Up
column21: Four widths, slim through extra-wide, which is rarer than it should be in a leather sneaker. It is flat and unstructured — a clean plimsoll shape done in leather, not a cushioned trainer.
A proper vulcanised plimsoll, so it creases and softens the way canvas is supposed to. The footbed lifts out if you wear an orthotic, and it comes in a true wide.
The retro runner with a visible midsole — chunkier than a court shoe, which is the point when you are balancing a wide trouser. Full-grain leather, so it holds its shape rather than collapsing.

column17: off white canvas, black suede, white/tan/black suede, deep olive, french burgundy, leopard calf hair + 6 more
column21: Twelve colourways of one shape, from plain black suede to leopard, so you choose how much attention it asks for. Medium and wide both, which almost nothing at this price offers.
The cleanest white leather sneaker in this group — tapered toe, low collar, nothing else going on. It runs narrow, so take the next size up if you are between sizes.
Real leather at eighty dollars, in the white low-top shape that goes with everything you already own. The contrast panel is the only detail, and it is enough.

column3: Vintage Wash Tencel Roll Sleeve Tunic Dress
column21: Sixty dollars for a Tencel tunic dress that resists wrinkling, shrinking and static, which is the whole argument for packing it. The collar and half placket give it enough shape to read deliberate rather than thrown on.

column17: flax, white, sand, deep navy, black, french blue, chambray stripe, classic mini gingham + 7 more
column21: Fifteen colours of a proper European linen button-front, and it runs into plus sizes. The belt comes off, so it works cinched at the waist or straight down as a column.

column17: navy, black, forest green planted meadows, storm blue boden spot, raw umber zebra swirl
column21: Boden cut this in three separate lengths — petite, regular and long — so the hem lands where it should instead of where it happens to. Cotton-modal jersey, side pockets, a high notch neck: the dress you keep by the door.

Linen with three percent stretch, which is the detail that stops it creasing into a map by lunchtime. Sizes 00 through 40, and the hi-low hem drops well below the knee at the back — worth checking against your height.

column17: dawn sky, ripe mango, blue starling, canvas, sways of palm, black
column21: A smocked bodice with a tie at the bust does what a zip never can — it adjusts to you across a whole day. Ruffled neckline, so it is tagged accordingly; if you have ruled ruffles out, this one stays hidden.

Four separately drafted fits, each with its own finished length — real pattern work rather than grading up. Misses, petite, plus and plus petite. Cotton corduroy, so it has weight and holds an A-line properly.
A navy cotton column with side slits and almost nothing else going on. That restraint is the point — it takes whatever shoes and jewellery you put with it and never argues.

Hemp and Tencel behaves like linen without the creasing, which is the trick this dress is built on. The flutter sleeve means it is tagged for ruffles. Runs small in the bust — size up if you are between.
The slimmest cut here, and the appliqué buttons down the placket are what lift it above a plain striped shirtdress. Hand wash only, which is unusual for cotton and worth knowing before you buy.

column3: By Anthropologie Peregrine Puff-Sleeve Midi Dress
column21: Brown plaid with a fully smocked bodice, and it pulls on — no zip, no buttons, nothing to fasten. Puff sleeves, tagged as such. One colourway only, so there is no fallback if it sells through.

column17: olive floral field spaced, denim blue delicate trail, almond milk geo, french navy flecked garden, black
column21: A proper tea dress — collar, seamed waist, floral, midi — but cut in jersey rather than a woven, so it travels and washes. Puff sleeves are the defining detail, tagged accordingly. Petite and long fits both offered.

Eyelet gives you texture and airflow in the same fabric, which is why it has outlasted a century of hot summers. Sleeveless with a real shoulder rather than a strap, and it comes in four separately drafted fits.
Buttoned through it is a shirtdress; worn open with the belt off it is nearly a coat. That double life is what makes the price make sense. Unlined viscose, so it wants a slip in bright light.

column3: Jardin Stripe Cotton Poplin Mitchell Dress
column21: Cotton poplin, fully lined, with a drawstring waist and real pockets — a dress that survives a whole day out. Sized XXS to XXXL, and puff sleeved, tagged accordingly.

The splurge, and unusually it is a linen day dress rather than an occasion piece — hand embroidery and crochet trim on 100% linen. Dry clean only is the real cost of ownership here, so go in knowing that.
